newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close firmer as banks strengthen.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close firmer as banks strengthen.

text.p: Toronto's stock market ended on a firmer note in healthy turnover on Thursday, bouncing back from Wednesday's weakness on the back of stronger bank issues.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index added 14.57 points to close at 6512.71. Trading was brisk at 102 million shares worth C$1.5 billion ($1.1 billion).
"Nice little rebound," said Dunnery Best, Midland Walwyn Capital's director of private client investing. "Barring the incalculable, this market is in pretty solid condition.
Eight of Toronto's 14 sub-groups rose, led by transportation, banks, media and consumer products.
The base metals sector declined, along with conglomerates and oils.
Advancing stocks beat out decliners 504 to 469, while 310 issues closed even.

Among hot stocks, theater company Cineplex Odeon Corp. added 0.17 to 2.62 on more than half a million shares. Reports in Variety and the Hollywood Reporter cited unidentified sources as saying that Cineplex was in merger talks with Loews Theaters, an arm of Sony Corp.
If combined, they would rank as North America's second largest movie theater chain.
Mutual funds manager Trimark Financial Corp. jumped 3.75 to a 52-week high of 63 in active dealings.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, Canada's second biggest bank, rose 0.45 to 34.70.
Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. slipped 1.45 to 30 after announcing on Thursday plans for C$600 million ($433 million) worth of medium-term notes.
